lines.text: An ambulance is coming toward you with its siren on… and right as it passes, the pitch suddenly drops.
Sound is a wave of pressure. Each time the siren sounds, a ring of pressure spreads out through the air… one after another, always at the same rhythm.
But if the siren is moving, every new ring starts from a spot a little further ahead.
So in front of the ambulance, the waves get squeezed together… and behind it, they get stretched apart.
And that's exactly what you hear.
If you're in front, more waves reach you every second… a higher pitch. If you're behind, fewer reach you… a lower pitch.
A seven-hundred-hertz siren at a hundred and eight kilometers an hour sounds like seven hundred sixty-seven coming toward you… and six hundred forty-four going away. A drop of about three notes.
But the siren never changed. It's always making the exact same sound. The only thing that changes is how many waves reach you each second.
Now… what if the vehicle goes as fast as its own sound?
Then it catches up with its own waves… and they all pile up into a single wall.
That's breaking the sound barrier… and that bang is a sonic boom.
And light does exactly the same thing.
A light source moving away reaches us stretched… shifted toward red. One coming closer reaches us squeezed… shifted toward blue.
Our neighbor, Andromeda, is coming toward us. Its light is shifted blue.
But almost every other galaxy… is shifted red. They're all moving away from us.
That's how, in nineteen twenty-nine, we discovered the universe is expanding.
The same trick that drops the pitch of an ambulance… showed us that the entire universe is growing.
